t: A French duchy around Dijon, Beaune and Chalon, ruled by a Capetian line from 1032 to 1361.
Cîteaux, founded near Dijon in 1098, made Burgundy the birthplace of the Cistercian order and of famous monastic vineyards.
Its Valois dukes built a wider Burgundian State; after Charles the Bold fell at Nancy in 1477, France annexed the duchy.
dyk: In 1395 Duke Philip the Bold ordered the Gamay grape uprooted from Burgundy’s vineyards, calling it a ‘very bad and disloyal’ plant, in favour of Pinot noir.
ev: Richard the Justiciar is recognised as duke of Burgundy
Henry I of France grants the duchy to his brother Robert, founding the Capetian line
Robert of Molesme founds Cîteaux, mother house of the Cistercian order
Duke Philip of Rouvres dies of plague and the Capetian line ends
John II grants Burgundy to his son Philip the Bold
Philip the Good founds the Order of the Golden Fleece
The Treaty of Arras reconciles Burgundy and France
Charles the Bold dies at Nancy and Louis XI occupies the duchy
